title: Minutes show what happened and put no words in mouths; a decision is finalised in one session (2026-11-27)

sections.name: narrative
sections.label: Narrative
sections.content:
We should probably establish rules for minutes.

Minutes need to show what happened in a meeting, they should not put words into people's mouths.
However, this allows for historical context, allowing a summary to better understand what is being said and minimise misrepresentation. This makes provenance important.

In practice we have learned that decisions can take place outside of meetings, so a session can be a meeting, but not necessarily. A decision may also be part of many meetings... but should only be finalised in one session.
